beats.say: 32 gigabytes: Nintendo Switch cartridges pack digital worlds, taste awful
That data capacity spans from one to 32 gigabytes, matching common phone storage on a tiny card.
Rather than standard optical discs found in classic home systems, these portable games use dedicated flash-based ROM cards.
Nintendo designed the hardware without any region lockout, meaning an identical card loads smoothly anywhere across the planet.
Yet players frequently discover an overwhelmingly dreadful taste whenever one touches their mouth.
The plain reason is these cartridges are purely physical electronic components, manufactured strictly for computing circuits instead of food.
Subscribe to Game Explained for more everyday tech secrets. Be honest, have you ever checked the taste yourself?
